novel_features.name: Cross-property mover board
novel_features.description: One report covering every verified property: top pages and queries by absolute click delta in the last window, with per-site rollup rows.
novel_features.rationale: Requires UNION across all sites' synced rows plus delta computation — no single API call expresses it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever you need to compare performance across multiple Search Console properties without N round trips.

novel_features.name: Keyword cannibalization
novel_features.description: Find queries where 2+ pages on the same site rank in the top 20 competing for the same intent; reports impression split and CTR drag.
novel_features.rationale: GROUP BY (site, query) HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT page) > 1 is structurally impossible against the single-call API.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when planning content consolidation or canonical fixes — surfaces internal SERP competition the GSC UI hides.

novel_features.name: Query decay watch
novel_features.description: Queries whose impressions or clicks have steadily declined over a rolling N-week window, ranked by absolute click loss.
novel_features.rationale: Linear-fit slope across 16 months of daily rows in SQLite; the live API has no slope endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catch gradual ranking erosion before it becomes a missing-traffic emergency.

novel_features.name: Coverage drift
novel_features.description: Diff successive URL-inspection snapshots: pages whose coverageState, lastCrawlTime, or googleCanonical changed since last sync.
novel_features.rationale: urlInspection.inspect is single-shot; only a local snapshot history can express drift.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Spot silent deindexings within hours of the next sync instead of weeks later from a stakeholder.

novel_features.name: Opportunity with baseline
novel_features.description: Today's quick-wins (positions 4-20, high-impression / low-CTR) joined to prior daily snapshots so each row carries the date the page entered the opportunity zone.
novel_features.rationale: Live API can compute a snapshot but cannot say when a page first became an opportunity — that requires history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets agents distinguish fresh opportunities (worth a refresh) from chronic ones (already triaged).

novel_features.name: New (and lost) queries
novel_features.description: Queries that appeared this week with material impressions and were absent in the prior trailing window; --lost inverts.
novel_features.rationale: LEFT JOIN against the prior window — anti-join requires persistent state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Aki's 'what's new since my last visit' loop without burning quota on full re-pulls.

novel_features.name: Indexing-issue triage
novel_features.description: Non-INDEXED pages from url_inspections joined against the last 30 days of impressions, ranked by traffic lost.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-table join between coverage state and historical impressions is the whole product; neither table alone is enough.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Fix the broken pages that actually drive traffic, not whatever was inspected most recently.

novel_features.name: Page momentum
novel_features.description: Pages whose 7-day clicks exceed (or fall below) their trailing 28-day daily average by N×, sorted by absolute lift.
novel_features.rationale: Windowed aggregation across daily rows in SQLite.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Spot rising stars and collapsing pages in one pass instead of eyeballing the GSC UI's compare mode.

novel_features.name: Territorial shift
novel_features.description: For each query, change in country and device mix week-over-week; flags queries whose geo or device split moved more than N points.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-time pivot on (query × country × device) requires stored history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Diagnose 'why did our US traffic drop' or 'mobile shift' questions in one command.

novel_features.name: Search-appearance breakdown
novel_features.description: Per-page or per-query breakdown of clicks/impressions by searchAppearance (featured snippet, sitelinks, video, FAQ rich result), with gain/loss flags across windows.
novel_features.rationale: The searchAppearance dimension is mutually exclusive with others in a single query, so cross-time tracking requires our isolated sync path.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catch lost rich-result eligibility (featured snippets, sitelinks) before traffic drops.

novel_features.name: Sitemap health
novel_features.description: Cross-snapshot diff on per-property sitemap state; flags new errors, new warnings, and indexed-vs-submitted ratio drops.
novel_features.rationale: sitemaps.list/get is point-in-time; the regression flag requires our local history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surface sitemap regressions in your weekly status email instead of next quarter's audit.

narrative.headline: Every Search Console feature, plus a local SQLite store that turns one-shot API calls into time-series insights no other GSC tool ships.
narrative.value_prop: Sync your search analytics, sites, sitemaps, and URL inspection state into a local store, then run cross-time queries the live API cannot express: query decay, keyword cannibalization, coverage drift, opportunity-with-baseline, and a cross-property mover board. Every command supports --json, --select, --csv, --dry-run, and ships an MCP server out of the box.
narrative.auth_narrative: OAuth2 with the `webmasters` (or `webmasters.readonly`) scope. Two paths: (1) run `google-search-console-pp-cli auth login` for the interactive OAuth2 flow and the CLI will store and refresh tokens for you; (2) for headless / CI environments, mint an access token elsewhere and set `GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_OAUTH2C` in env. Easiest token source for local dev: `gcloud auth login` against a project with the Search Console API enabled, then `export GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_OAUTH2C=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)`. Run `auth status` to confirm the binary can read your credential.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI can mint an access token via gcloud or service account before anything else.
List your verified properties so you have a site URL to point sync at.
Backfill 90 days of search-analytics rows and current url-inspection state into the local SQLite store.
Pages on positions 4-20 with high impressions and low CTR that entered the opportunity zone within the last 14 days.
Cross-property mover board: largest click deltas this week across every verified site, with a per-site rollup.

troubleshoots.fix: Run `gcloud auth login` then `gcloud auth print-access-token` to confirm a token mints; the CLI shells out to the same command.
Make sure the authed account is verified on the property in Search Console, or pass `--credentials` to a service account that is.
Retry with `--throttle slow`; default quotas are 1,200 QPM per project, 30,000 QPD.
`searchAppearance` is mutually exclusive with all other dimensions in a single call; request it alone or use the `appearance` command which handles the split.

troubleshoots.symptom: Sync fills in zero rows for the last 2-3 days
troubleshoots.fix: GSC search analytics finalize ~3 days late; sync only writes through `today-3` by default. Use `--data-state all` to include preliminary rows.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI whenever a task needs more than one Search Console call at a time — period-over-period analysis, cross-property roll-ups, drift detection, or any question that requires comparing today's data to history. The local SQLite store and SQL/FTS surface make it the right tool for agent loops that want deterministic 'what changed since last visit' answers without burning API quota. For one-shot lookups (sites list, single URL inspection) a generic HTTP client is fine; reach for this CLI when persistence pays for itself.

recipes.explanation: Pages that flipped from INDEXED to anything else since the last sync — the change Priya finds out from sales reps weeks later today.
